title: Rosalind and the Letter
premise: Estate lawyer Beatrix Eastwick is summoned to Thornfield House to read the will of Rosalind Vane, a woman who vanished seven years ago and was declared dead in absentia. The will is dated after her disappearance, and enclosed with it is a diary whose entries continue past the date she went missing — proof that someone has been writing as Rosalind for years, or that Rosalind never left at all. As Beatrix traces the diary's hand through forged signatures, a hidden second identity, and a family fortune built on a lie, she realizes the killer is feeding her clues from inside the investigation itself. In the end Beatrix lures the killer into revealing themselves at a staged reading of the will, uncovering that Rosalind faked her death to escape her husband and was murdered years later when she tried to reclaim her name; justice arrives too late for love, but not too late for truth.
about_author: Sebastian Oyelaran is a former probate clerk who spent a decade handling contested wills in England's Home Counties before turning to fiction full-time. He writes mysteries about paper trails, dead women who refuse to stay quiet, and the lawyers who listen.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Beatrix Eastwick receives an envelope containing Rosalind Vane's will, postmarked last month though Rosalind vanished seven years ago and was declared dead. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: Thornfield House
chapters.summary: Beatrix travels to the decaying Vane estate to meet the family contesting the will. Her cold husband Edmund greets her with rehearsed grief. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: dread beneath polite surfaces.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: The solicitor's clerk produces a diary found sealed in the house safe; its final entries are dated three years after Rosalind disappeared. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: vertigo — the dead writing on.

chapters.title: A Hand She Recognizes
chapters.summary: Beatrix compares the diary's handwriting to old legal documents and finds it flawless — too flawless, like forgery practiced to perfection. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: suspicion sharpening into method.

chapters.title: Edmund's Grief, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Edmund Vane gives a polished interview about his lost wife, but slips on a detail only the diary contains. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: first real crack in the widower's mask.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Waited
chapters.summary: Rosalind's sister Cordelia hints that Rosalind was unhappy, trapped, planning something before she vanished. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: sympathy complicating the case.

chapters.title: Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Someone has torn pages from the diary between two dates; the binding shows removal, not loss. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: violation — the killer is ahead of her.

chapters.title: The Case File
chapters.summary: Beatrix obtains the original missing-persons file and notices the investigating officer closed it suspiciously fast. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: institutional rot revealed.

chapters.title: Inspector Hale
chapters.summary: Retired Inspector Hale admits he was pressured to close the case but refuses to say by whom. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: an ally afraid of his own memory.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Testimony
chapters.summary: An aging groundskeeper recalls seeing Rosalind's car leave the night she vanished — with two people inside. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: hope that quickly turns to dread.

chapters.title: Ink and Water
chapters.summary: Forensic analysis dates the late diary entries' ink correctly — meaning either genuine time travel of a sort, or meticulous staging. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under her theory.

chapters.title: What the Will Gives Away
chapters.summary: The will leaves everything to a beneficiary named only as 'R.' — a codicil no lawyer would draft by accident. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: realizing the document itself is a message.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Warning
chapters.summary: Cordelia begs Beatrix to drop the case, then recants, terrified. Someone has been watching the house. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: fear arriving at her own doorstep.

chapters.title: The Second Identity
chapters.summary: Beatrix uncovers bank records showing 'Rosamund Vale,' a woman with Rosalind's handwriting, living quietly in Cornwall until four years ago. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: exhilaration — Rosalind lived.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Among Rosamund's effects, unsent letters to Cordelia describe a marriage built on control and a plan to disappear. POV: Beatrix (reading letters). Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead.

chapters.title: The Return
chapters.summary: Records show Rosamund Vale returned north four years ago — toward Thornfield — and then vanishes from all records again. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the trap closing backward in time.

chapters.title: Hale Breaks Silence
chapters.summary: Inspector Hale confesses Edmund's family solicitor pressured him to close the file; that solicitor was Beatrix's own mentor. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: betrayal close to home.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Searching her mentor's old office, Beatrix finds payments from Edmund Vane logged the week after the disappearance. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief and fury entwined.

chapters.title: An Attempted Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix's hotel room is searched; the diary nearly stolen. She begins keeping duplicate notes hidden off-site. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: The Diary's Last Entry
chapters.summary: The true final entry, in different ink, reads: 'He knows. If I stop writing, look where the roses were planted.' POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: chill of a voice reaching across years.

chapters.title: Where the Roses Were Planted
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Hale excavate the rose garden at night and find nothing — but disturbed earth older than the beds suggests the body was moved. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: hope deferred.

chapters.title: Cordelia Disappears
chapters.summary: Cordelia misses their meeting; her cottage shows signs of hurried departure, staged or real. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: guilt and urgency doubling.

chapters.title: The Lake House
chapters.summary: Following property records, Beatrix finds a lake house deeded to 'R. Vale' — and signs someone has been living there recently. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the past still warm.

chapters.title: Cordelia Found
chapters.summary: Cordelia is discovered alive, drugged and dumped; she saw her captor's face but only through a mask. She whispers one word: 'inside.' POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: relief shadowed by worse knowledge.

chapters.title: Inside Means Staff
chapters.summary: Beatrix narrows suspects to those with access to both estates and files: the current caretaker, the family solicitor's junior, and Edmund's new wife. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: paranoia among allies.

chapters.title: The Junior Partner
chapters.summary: The junior solicitor is found dead, staged as suicide, holding a page of the missing diary. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: horror — the killer erasing the trail through people.

chapters.title: Reading the Killer's Hand
chapters.summary: Beatrix realizes the forged diary entries contain deliberate errors matching the killer's own handwriting quirks — a taunt, or a confession waiting to be read. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: turning fear into leverage.

chapters.title: Edmund Confronted
chapters.summary: Beatrix accuses Edmund directly; he neither denies nor confirms, only says Rosalind 'chose to leave twice.' POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: loathing sharpened by doubt.

chapters.title: The New Wife's Story
chapters.summary: Edmund's wife Imogen reveals she was hired to impersonate Rosalind's habits, coached by someone who knew them intimately. POV: Imogen. Emotional beat: a pawn awakening.

chapters.title: Who Knew Her Best
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the coaching, Beatrix identifies the only person with total access to Rosalind's private life: her childhood companion, now the estate caretaker, Thomas Wren. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: heartbreak — the closest friend.

chapters.title: Thomas Wren's Devotion
chapters.summary: Flashback chapters via Wren's seized journals reveal obsessive love for Rosalind and rage when she chose disappearance over him. POV: Wren (journal). Emotional beat: love rotted into ownership.

chapters.title: The Night She Came Back
chapters.summary: Wren's journal describes Rosalind returning four years ago to reclaim her identity — and Wren killing her to keep her 'his' forever, then forging the diary onward. POV: Wren (journal). Emotional beat: revulsion and pity.

chapters.title: Burial Beneath the Roses
chapters.summary: Wren moved the body to the lake house grounds; Hale obtains a warrant and remains are found. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grim vindication.

chapters.title: Wren Vanishes
chapters.summary: Warned by a leak inside the police, Wren disappears with Cordelia as hostage, leaving a final diary entry addressed to Beatrix by name. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the hunt inverted.

chapters.title: The Staged Reading
chapters.summary: Beatrix publicly announces a formal reading of the will at Thornfield, knowing Wren cannot resist attending the ending of Rosalind's story. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: cold courage.

chapters.title: Trap at Thornfield
chapters.summary: During the reading, Beatrix reads aloud the forged entries' errors, forcing Wren to break cover to silence her; Cordelia is freed in the chaos. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into command.

chapters.title: Confession Among the Roses
chapters.summary: Cornered in the garden, Wren confesses with terrible tenderness, believing he kept Rosalind safe from the world. Hale arrests him. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: pity without absolution.

chapters.title: Edmund's Reckoning
chapters.summary: With Wren's testimony, Edmund faces charges for the cover-up payments; the estate passes to Cordelia under the true intent of Rosalind's codicil. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: justice, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Among final effects Beatrix finds Rosalind's last unsent letter — to no one, to herself — choosing freedom over safety, written the night she died. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: mourning a stranger she came to love.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: Beatrix writes the report that finally closes the case properly, visits the grave marked with Rosalind's real name, and burns her duplicate notes. Some stories belong to the dead alone. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: release.
